articles.title: Indonesia seeks at least 70% of mining returns for the state
articles.summary: The Northern Miner reported on 16 November 2026 that President Prabowo Subianto instructed ministers that the state should receive at least 70 percent of the benefit from mining permits, and said that if necessary shares should be state-controlled. The report said the presidency did not define how the share would be measured or give an implementation timetable, and that Prabowo also called for exports to pass through a designated agency.

articles.title: EU lists 113 individuals and entities, including nearly 50 Russian banks
articles.summary: On 16 November 2026 the Council of the EU imposed an asset freeze and related restrictions on 12 individuals and 101 entities, including nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, energy companies and buyers of Russian-origin crude oil products in the UAE, China, Seychelles and Oman. Listings of this kind can affect payment channels and counterparties for trade involving Russia.

articles.title: Gabriel Resources warns of insolvency after ICSID committee rejects Roșia Montană annulment bid
articles.summary: Mining South East Europe reported on 15 November 2026 that an ICSID ad hoc committee dismissed Canadian company Gabriel Resources' application to annul the 2024 award that rejected its claims against Romania over the Roșia Montană project. The company said the decision leaves in force an order to pay about $10 million of Romania's costs plus interest and has material implications for its ability to continue as a going concern.

articles.title: IMF says Senegal must implement budget framework to win approval of $2.2bn programme
articles.summary: Reuters, in a report published by TimesLIVE on 12 November 2026, said the IMF wants Senegal to complete a budget framework, corrective measures on misreported debt and financing assurances from partners before its board approves a $2.2 billion programme. The report said the programme underpins Senegal's strategy to rework its debt and that the official creditor committee had not yet been formed.

articles.title: IMF holds new talks with Lebanon on bank restructuring strategy
articles.summary: The National reported on 12 November 2026 that IMF staff held a new round of talks with Lebanon focused on banking-sector restructuring, with a law distributing losses between the state, central bank, commercial banks and depositors still a sticking point. The report noted Lebanon defaulted on its debt in March 2020 and that the IMF has said a 2027 budget and medium-term fiscal framework are needed for any agreement.

articles.title: Canada to merge Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada
articles.summary: Global Trade Review reported on 11 November 2026 that Canada's 2026 Budget plans to merge EDC and BDC into a single federal development bank, with the Canadian Commercial Corporation becoming an EDC subsidiary. EDC said there is no confirmed merger date, it remains fully operational, and it does not anticipate changes to existing contractual commitments with customers.

articles.title: Myanmar extends export earnings retention period from 30 to 45 days
articles.summary: Xinhua reported on 10 November 2026 that the Central Bank of Myanmar extended, from 30 to 45 days, the period exporters may retain the discretionary portion of export earnings in private foreign-currency accounts. The previous 30-day rule dated from a notification of 16 August 2022.

articles.title: Canada lists 38 entities and 24 individuals under its Russia sanctions regulations
articles.summary: Global Affairs Canada announced on 9 November 2026 that Canada is listing 38 entities and 24 individuals under the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations, targeting defence-industry, ballistic missile and cyber actors and financial enablers including crypto exchanges. The release says the measures are also intended to raise the economic costs of Russia’s war against Ukraine.
